[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-13.87): Good afternoon, Rachel. Daniel Lim here. Thanks for setting aside a few minutes for the call. I'm at my desk and have your file open. We can keep this brief, so you won't need to come down to the branch.
[seg_0002] Client (14.27-29.10): Hi Daniel, thank you. Telephone is much easier for me, especially between meetings. Let me give you my particulars first. For your records, my FIN is G nine two eight triple six nine Q. My date of birth is the thirteenth of August nineteen eighty-two.
[seg_0003] Advisor (29.50-55.20): Thank you, Rachel. I'll keep the discussion concise rather than go through a long presentation. From our earlier conversation, I've recorded the following. Your objective is to earn investment income and diversify your personal portfolio, while keeping the option to sell before maturity if your circumstances change. Are you willing to accept investment losses in exchange for the opportunity to earn income?
[seg_0004] Client (55.60-67.06): Yes, I am willing to accept investment losses for the opportunity to earn income, though I prefer predictability. I've got a little time now, but I need to leave for another appointment shortly. Please keep to the main points.
[seg_0005] Advisor (67.46-95.78): Certainly. I recommend Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 because its scheduled interest payments support your income objective, and corporate debt can help diversify your personal portfolio. With Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, the issuer could run into financial trouble and miss interest payments or fail to repay the principal. If market interest rates rise, the bond's resale price could also fall before maturity.
[seg_0006] Client (96.19-100.04): Can you guarantee the returns? I would prefer certainty if that's available.
[seg_0007] Advisor (100.44-119.23): No, I can't guarantee the returns. What you receive depends on the issuer meeting its obligations and on market conditions if you sell early. You could lose some or even all of the capital you invest in this bond. The transaction fee is 0.25% of the transaction amount.
[seg_0008] Client (119.63-132.34): Before I give you the details, a quick administrative point. I'm travelling quite a bit at the moment, and correspondence gets scattered across different folders. I'd rather have everything accessible through the usual secure channel than carry papers around.
[seg_0009] Advisor (132.74-146.19): We can keep the correspondence in the usual secure channel. You can access it while you're away. For general questions about where to find documents, you can also contact me by telephone instead of making a branch visit.
[seg_0010] Client (146.59-173.88): That's convenient. I keep my personal paperwork separate from the company files, so I don't want bank correspondence buried among the office emails. Anyway, here are my details for today. The product I want to transact in is Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031. I want to buy the bond. Please use US dollars as the currency for this transaction. I use Chinese yuan only as a mental reference when comparing the income with my overseas business receipts, not as the currency for this transaction.
[seg_0011] Advisor (174.28-188.77): Thank you. On the correspondence side, I'll leave the office contact arrangements as they are. There's no need to involve your staff in our telephone discussions. You can reach me directly for help navigating the document inbox.
[seg_0012] Client (189.17-198.77): The amount I want to commit to this transaction is 150,000. Please set the quantity at 10,000 units. Please place a limit order with a limit price of 15 US dollars.
[seg_0013] Advisor (199.17-209.44): Thank you, Rachel. For any follow-up contact, is an afternoon call generally easier while you're travelling, or would you rather we arrange a time by secure message first?
[seg_0014] Client (209.84-220.42): Please message first. My calendar changes quite often, and sometimes I'm in a taxi or at a meeting when the phone rings. If we agree on a slot, I can find somewhere quiet and have my documents ready.
[seg_0015] Advisor (220.82-234.18): Sure, we'll arrange a suitable slot through the secure channel. If you need help locating correspondence, let me know which section you're looking at. Please don't send passwords or access codes in a message.
[seg_0016] Client (234.58-244.22): Okay, that arrangement works for my schedule. I'll check the inbox when I'm back at the hotel, rather than try to sort things out on my phone between appointments. Thanks for keeping the call short.
[seg_0017] Advisor (244.62-251.76): You're welcome. I'll let you get to your appointment. Have a good afternoon, Rachel, and safe travels.
[seg_0018] Client (252.16-255.71): Thanks, Daniel. Speak another time. Bye.

call_intent.reasoning: The advisor recommends Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 in seg_0005 based on the client's investment objectives, establishing the advisory intent. The subsequent buy order in seg_0010/seg_0012 follows this recommendation and is covered under advisory rather than execution_only. Additionally, enquiry intent is reached in seg_0006 where the client asks product information questions about guaranteed returns, as well as discussing service preferences for document delivery.

the sales of riskier products to these clients. Instances were also noted where clients were 
told by their RMs that the risk profiling exercise was a paper exercise. These observations 
reflect RMs’ lack of risk consciousness and adopting a perfunctory approach towards the 
risk profiling exercise. MAS expects PBs to inculcate the right mindset and understanding 
amongst front office staff with regard to clients’ safeguards and their duty to act in the 
interest of their clients. PBs should pay  attention to changes in clien ts’ profiles and 
implement controls to mitigate the risk of clients being unduly influenced to take on 
higher risk profiles or invest in products beyond their intended risk appetites. Examples of 
such controls include regular analyses of migration of clients’ profiles to identify unusual 
trends and patterns, and perform ance of independent sampling checks (e.g. listening to 
voice logs) to assess whether RMs inappropriately influenced clients to adopt a higher risk 
tolerance.

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
